title: VWP Analysis Attestation
description: A structured record of a model-assisted review procedure performed over a defined evidence scope. Attestations never affect package validity; findings route to humans via required dispositions.

performedBy.description: Person, team, or service that ran the review procedure. Same shape conventions as provenance createdBy.

model.description: The exact model that performed the analysis. Recording exact identity lets consumers confirm the challenger differs from the preparer models recorded in provenance.

name.description: Exact model identifier as published by the provider, not a family or marketing name.

version.description: Model version or snapshot date; use the provider's most specific identifier available.

role.description: What the model did, e.g. 'challenger', 'consistency review'.

scope.description: The declared review scope: exactly which evidence bytes were examined and which claims were challenged.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the evidence bytes as examined, pinning the review to exact content.

claimsChallenged.description: Claim ids the procedure was directed at. MAY be empty for scope-wide procedures not aimed at specific claims.

procedure.description: Human-readable description of the review procedure the model was asked to perform.

subject.description: The exact package content this review examined, stamped by the server (never supplied by the attesting model). A review speaks only for the content it saw: when the package changes afterwards, consumers enforcing a review requirement MUST treat this attestation as stale rather than carrying it forward.

contentDigest.description: Digest of the package CONTENT parts (excluding approvals, renderings and validations) as examined.

versionHash.description: The package version pinned at review time, when one existed.

requiresDisposition.description: Always true: every finding requires a human disposition. Findings route to humans, never silently into conclusions.

limitations.description: What the procedure could not assess (evidence out of scope, questions requiring professional judgment, model constraints).

dispositions.description: Human decisions on findings. A disposition is a human act; it MUST NOT be produced by the attesting model.
